blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — clonidine transdermal administration
stem: A client is starting a clonidine transdermal system. Which statement by the client shows correct understanding of application?

options.A: I will apply a new system every 7 days to a hairless area of intact skin on the upper outer arm or chest and rotate the application site.
options.B: I will replace the system every 24 hours and reuse the same skin site so the medication is absorbed consistently from one location.
options.C: I will apply the system over irritated or broken skin because damaged skin improves medication delivery and shortens the onset of action.
options.D: I will place each new system directly over the previous site because changing locations can interrupt the weekly clonidine dose.

rationale: Current clonidine transdermal labeling directs application once every 7 days to a hairless area of intact skin on the upper outer arm or chest, with each new application placed at a different skin site. Therefore A is correct. B uses an incorrect daily replacement interval and fails site rotation, C uses nonintact skin, and D contradicts the site-rotation instruction.
educational_objective: Apply clonidine transdermal systems once every 7 days to hairless intact skin on the upper outer arm or chest and rotate application sites.
source_document_title: Clonidine Transdermal System, USP — Prescribing Information
source_version_date: Current DailyMed label published April 2026; current page rechecked 2026-08-26
source_locator: Dosage and Administration: apply once every 7 days to a hairless area of intact skin on the upper outer arm or chest; each new application should be on a different skin site.
source_claim_supported: Clonidine transdermal system is applied once every 7 days to hairless intact skin on the upper outer arm or chest, with site rotation.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: prepare/administer medications safely and educate clients about medication administration.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all options as complete application plans of comparable length.
Removed isolated absolute-word cueing and used a current 2026 DailyMed label.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current labeling; B has the wrong interval/site reuse, C uses nonintact skin, and D contradicts rotation guidance. No second defensible answer remains.
